question: True or false: in a 2007 study of 100,000 data-centre disks, drives were replaced several times more often than their ratings implied?
answer: True. Datasheets promised mean times to failure of up to 1.5 million hours, implying under 1% of drives failing a year; the sites replaced typically 2 to 4%, and up to 13%. The ratings came from short tests on new drives in clean conditions. A warehouse of five-year-old disks is a different population.
move: Ask which units were tested before trusting a figure about yours.
trap: False, trusting a rating as if it measured drives like yours.
reference: Schroeder & Gibson, Disk failures in the real world: What does an MTTF of 1,000,000 hours mean to you?, USENIX FAST, 2007
